text:
maya: Hey team — hit a weird one after bundling our Node service with esbuild. Calls to the Redwood TS SDK suddenly return 401s in staging, and runtime types look mangled. Unbundled dev build works fine. Anyone seen auth break only after bundle?

support-eng: Oof. Can you paste your package.json exports + the esbuild command you used? Also any runtime error logs you see in the container?

maya: Paste: ```json
{
  \"name\": \"our-service\",\n  \"version\": \"0.3.0\",\n  \"main\": \"dist/cjs/index.js\",\n  \"module\": \"dist/esm/index.js\",\n  \"types\": \"dist/index.d.ts\",\n  \"exports\": {\n    \".\": {\n      \"import\": \"./dist/esm/index.js\",\n      \"require\": \"./dist/cjs/index.js\"\n    \n    }\n  }\n}\n```

and esbuild: `esbuild src/main.ts --bundle --outfile=dist/bundle.js --platform=node --target=node18 --format=cjs`

Error in logs (only in container): ```
TypeError: RedwoodSDK is not a function
    at Object.<anonymous> (/app/dist/bundle.js:12345:12)
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:999:30)
```
but stack is minified by bundling. Also downstream requests to our backend (which sign and forward API key) show empty Authorization header which matches the 401 on Redwood API.

alex: Two quick possibilities — bundler picked the wrong entry (exports.import -> esm) while you forced cjs output; esbuild may rewrite interop shims and drop a `.default` or named export. That can convert an exported client factory into an object and calling it yields TypeError. If the SDK's auth helper is on the default export, it could be skipped, leaving an uninitialized header helper -> empty auth -> 401.

support-eng: Can you run a small repro locally without your app glue? Create a tiny repo that `require('your-bundle')` or import the SDK directly from `dist/*` and show `console.log(Object.keys(require('./dist/bundle.js')))` or `node --trace-warnings -e \"const r=require('./dist/bundle.js'); console.log(typeof r)\"`. If that shows an object vs function, we found it.

maya: I ran `node -e \"const r = require('./dist/bundle.js'); console.log(Object.keys(r), r.default && typeof r.default)\"` and got: `[ 'default' ] , 'object'` — seems default is an object not a function.

jordan: Also check package-lock/yarn.lock for duplicate SDK versions. There was a case where lockfile hoisted a different minor version with a changed export shape. `npm ls @redwood/inference` or `pnpm list @redwood/inference` can show that.

patrick: Short-term workaround: force the runtime entry to the CJS build so require() gets the expected shape. In package.json try: \"exports\": { \".\": \"./dist/cjs/index.js\" } (temporarily remove conditional import/require map). Or change esbuild output to `--format=esm` and run under node with `--experimental-specifier-resolution=node` if you can. Both are stopgaps.

support-eng: Another option: add an explicit interop wrapper before bundling: in your src shim `const Redwood = require('./node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/cjs').default || require('./node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/cjs'); module.exports = Redwood;` Then bundle the shim.

alex: For longer-term fix we should validate SDK package fields — if the SDK publishes exports that the bundlers misinterpret, we need to add a `exports` entry that includes a `require` path that is canonical, and ensure `package.json#main` matches it. If you can share the SDK version, we can check release notes.

maya: SDK version: `@redwood/inference@1.2.0`. Pinning to 1.1.7 locally made the error go away in staging.

support-eng: Good to know. Can you open a minimal repro (public or private) or attach an anonymized bundle so we can inspect the AST? If you'd rather we escalate, we can open an internal issue with the infra/release team.

infra-bot: Incident created — #INC-2024-119: SDK bundling -> 401s after esbuild. Assigned to eng-runtime.

jordan: For types complaints: if your bundler collapsed declarations or they point to `dist/index.d.ts` but you only shipped `dist/esm/index.d.ts`, consumers can get missing types. Ensure your build emits both CJS + ESM .d.ts or use a single `types` entry that points to the public d.ts root. Also update `typesVersions` in package.json if you need TS path remapping for specific TS versions.

support-eng: Action items — maya: (1) try temporary exports override to force CJS and redeploy, (2) run `npm ls @redwood/inference` and paste output, (3) if possible attach tiny repro. We'll hold on escalation until we see repro, but since pin to 1.1.7 works, consider pinning in prod while we investigate.

maya: Will do steps now and report back. Thanks all :pray:

support-eng: If repro shows it's an SDK publishing problem, we'll open a release rollback/patch and coordinate with runtime to avoid cascading 401s.
